original_question: For the generalized Robin boundary-value problem in which the a priori L^{q**} bounds are derived from an embedding of D(a_S) into L^p(Omega) together with Moser iteration, are those resulting L^{q**} a priori bounds best possible?
target_in_paper: Section 7.2, Remark 12: "One could ask if the a priori bounds derived from (45) by Moser iteration are the best possible. Indeed they are."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the Robin part of the paper, the extra embedding hypothesis in the generalized Robin setting, the role of Moser iteration in producing higher Lebesgue-space a priori bounds, and the fact that the natural issue raised there is whether those bounds are optimal.
missing_details: The paper is not speaking about Robin problems in general, but about the generalized Robin boundary value problem (42) on an arbitrary open set Ω ⊂ R^d.

The Robin structure is encoded by a positive Borel measure μ on ∂Ω, the associated form a on H^1(Ω) (or its maximal closable part), and the maximal μ-admissible set S from Theorem 9; the relevant form is a_S with domain D(a_S).
The crucial extra hypothesis is precisely assumption (45), which replaces the Sobolev embedding used in the Dirichlet case; your draft alludes to it, but does not name it explicitly.

The question concerns the a priori Lebesgue bounds obtained from the Moser-iteration step in the proof of the Robin analogue of Theorem 2 / Theorem 10, not merely any bound coming from an arbitrary embedding D(a_S) into L^p(Ω).
The symbol q** should be defined as the endpoint Lebesgue exponent yielded by that iteration from assumption (45); in the draft it appears without definition.
The semilinearity and coerciveness assumptions are those carried over from Section 2, with the modifications stated in Section 7.2; the draft omits that scope condition.
The paper's formulation is about whether the bounds are 'best possible' in general, not about a special subclass of domains or measures.
Most importantly, the paper does not leave this as an open problem: Remark 12 answers the question affirmatively, citing Daners [Theorem 5.11].
refined_question: For the generalized Robin problem (42) on an arbitrary open set Ω ⊂ R^d, with Robin form a_S corresponding to the maximal μ-admissible set S from Theorem 9, and under the additional embedding hypothesis (45) that replaces the Sobolev embedding in the Moser-iteration argument, are the resulting a priori Lebesgue-space bounds for weak solutions—equivalently, the endpoint L^{q**}(Ω)-bound furnished by that iteration—optimal in general, or can the exponent q** be improved beyond the value obtained from (45)?
justification: The closest paper-faithful target is not an open problem in Section 6 and not an earlier Dirichlet-only theorem, but Remark 12 in Section 7.2. The nearby context is exactly the generalized Robin setup: Theorem 9 introduces the maximal μ-admissible set S and hence the relevant Robin form a_S; assumption (45) is singled out as the replacement for the Sobolev embedding in the Moser-iteration step; Theorem 10 states the resulting generalized existence theorem; and Remark 12 then asks precisely whether the a priori bounds obtained from (45) by Moser iteration are best possible, answering yes via Daners [Theorem 5.11].
